source_text: Ὅτι οὐ δεῖ ὑπηρέτην ἄρτον διδόναι, οὐδὲ ποτήριον εὐλογεῖν.
thought_title: Servants may not distribute bread or bless the cup
orientation: The council is issuing a short disciplinary canon about liturgical roles, after the opening of the canons.
pass_a_gloss: That it is not permitted for a servant to give bread, nor to bless the cup.

choices.why: The brief's cast identifies this as the liturgical attendant ranked below deacons; 'servant' keeps the plain literal sense without importing later subdeacon terminology.
Literal rendering of the infinitive phrase; the bread is the Eucharistic bread, but the source says only 'bread,' so the gloss keeps that bareness.
Literal; the cup is the Eucharistic cup, and 'bless' is the standard sense of εὐλογεῖν in liturgical contexts.
rejected: to say the blessing over the cup

choices.why: The impersonal δεῖ with negative expresses prohibition; 'it is not permitted' captures the canonical force better than a bare 'must not.'

pass_b_english: A servant is not permitted to give the bread or to bless the cup.
